long-sentence.label: Long sentence
long-sentence.why: This sentence has more than 25 words. Long sentences are easy to get lost in.
long-sentence.try: Split it into two sentences where you see "and," "but," or "which."

wall-of-text.label: Wall of text
wall-of-text.why: This paragraph is long (more than 5 sentences or 100 words). Readers skim past big blocks.
wall-of-text.try: Break it into two paragraphs, one idea each. Press Enter twice to start a new one.

passive.label: Passive voice
passive.why: Passive voice hides who did the action ("the form was sent").
passive.try: Say who did it: "I sent the form" instead of "the form was sent."

jargon.label: Jargon
jargon.why: This is office-speak a stranger might not understand.
jargon.try: Say it in everyday words, the way you'd explain it to a friend.

acronym.label: Unexplained acronym
acronym.why: The reader may not know what these letters stand for.
acronym.try: Spell it out the first time, then put the letters after it, like "Human Resources (HR)."

simpler.label: Simpler word available
simpler.why: There's a shorter, everyday word with the same meaning.

wordy.label: Wordy phrase
wordy.why: This phrase uses three or four words where one or two would do.

filler.label: Filler word
filler.why: Words like this add little meaning. Your sentence is stronger without it.
filler.try: Read the sentence without it. If the meaning doesn't change, leave it out.

adverb.label: Adverb
adverb.why: This -ly word props up a plain verb. One stronger verb says it better.
adverb.try: Pick one verb that does both jobs, like "hurried" instead of "walked quickly." Or cut the -ly word.

vague.label: Vague word
vague.why: This word is fuzzy. The reader can't tell the amount, the number, or what you mean.
vague.try: Use the real number, name, or item.

vague-date.label: Vague date or time
vague-date.why: "Soon" or "tomorrow" can mean a different day to each reader, and it changes depending on when it's read.
vague-date.try: Use a real date, like "Friday, Nov 6" or "by 3 p.m. Monday."

spelling.label: Spelling or grammar
spelling.why: This looks like a spelling or grammar mistake.
spelling.try: Check the spelling or grammar here. If the app has ideas, they're listed above.

slang.label: Slang or text-speak
slang.why: This is too casual for professional writing.
slang.try: Write the full word, like "thanks" instead of "thx" or "going to" instead of "gonna."

capital-start.label: Sentence starts lowercase
capital-start.why: Sentences should start with a capital letter.
capital-start.try: Make the first letter a capital.

lowercase-i.label: Lowercase "i"
lowercase-i.why: When you mean yourself, "I" is always a capital.

no-transition.label: No linking word
no-transition.why: This paragraph doesn't connect back to the one before it. That's a hint, not an error.
no-transition.try: Think about a linking word at the start, like "Also," "Because of this," or "Next."

missing-fact.label: Key fact not found
missing-fact.why: You listed this as a key fact in your plan, but it isn't in your writing yet.
missing-fact.try: Add it where it fits. If you already said it in other words, press It's fine.

goal-late.label: Main point comes late
goal-late.why: The goal in your plan doesn't seem to show up in your first two sentences. Most readers stop after those.
goal-late.try: Say what you want near the start, in your own words. If it's already there in other words, you can ignore this note.

missing-reader.label: Reader's name not found
missing-reader.why: You named your reader in your plan, but their name isn't in your writing.
missing-reader.try: Use their name near the start, like in the greeting.

missing-deadline.label: Deadline not found
missing-deadline.why: You set a deadline in your plan, but it isn't in your writing.
missing-deadline.try: Put the date where you say what you need, so the reader knows when.

no-ask.label: No clear next step
no-ask.why: Your ask doesn't tell the reader what to do next.
no-ask.try: Start with words like "Could you…," "Please…," or "I'd like to request…," and add a date.

harsh.label: Bossy or harsh wording
harsh.why: This can sound demanding or annoyed, even if you don't mean it that way.
harsh.try: Soften it: "Could you…" instead of "You must…," or "by Friday" instead of "immediately."

all-caps.label: ALL CAPS
all-caps.why: All capital letters read like shouting.
all-caps.try: Use normal capitals. If a point matters, say why it matters.

exclamations.label: Too many exclamation marks
exclamations.why: More than two exclamation marks can sound too excited or upset.
exclamations.try: Keep it to one or two. Let your words carry the feeling.

greeting-informal.label: Greeting too casual
greeting-informal.why: For this reader, a casual hello like "Hey" can come across as disrespectful.

greeting-name.label: Greeting missing their name
greeting-name.why: You know your reader's name. Using it is more personal and polite.
greeting-name.try: Add their name, like "Dear Ms. Alvarez,".

no-polite-close.label: No thank-you or polite close
no-polite-close.why: Your closing doesn't thank the reader or end with a polite sign-off.
no-polite-close.try: Add a thank-you like "Thank you for your help." and a sign-off like "Best regards,".
